messages.author: ae4e01c9cf4da161
messages.subject: Comparing two coefficient differences
parts:
Hi all,
I have a two regression models with different predicted variables but the same predictors.
I would like to test the hypothesis that in Model 1, x1 is a better predictor than x2, but that in Model 2 x2 is a better predictor than x1.

This is my code:

modelNoAtt <- '
y1~ a*x1 + b*x2
y2 ~ c*x1 + d*x2
# difference effects
diffA := (a - b)
diffB := (c - d)
diffAB := diffA-diffB
'

Would diffAB be a meaningful statistic?
Do you have any references for this kind of analysis?

Best,
Almog

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Comparing two coefficient differences
parts: Would diffAB be a meaningful statistic?
No, unless you additionally hypothesize that the degree to which Hypothesis 1 holds is greater than the degree to which Hypothesis 2 holds.
Do you have any references for this kind of analysis?

The restriktor package was designed to test inequality constraints like the ones you describe.  You can probably find references in the help pages.

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/restriktor/index.html
